caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a multi-series line plot showing training loss versus iteration for six model configurations, with a legend in the upper-right. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration” on a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 140,000 with major ticks at regular 20,000-iteration intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, ranging approximately from 2.4 to 3.4 with ticks at about 0.1 increments. Six colored solid lines (each with a faint, same-color shaded band around it indicating variability) are plotted: Vanilla (purple), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue), SepLLM (n=64) (orange), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red), and SepLLM (n=128) (dark blue). All curves start above about 3.4 near iteration 0, drop steeply within the early iterations, and then decline more gradually toward the end of training. By 140,000 iterations, the purple Vanilla curve is near ~2.45, the blue StrmLLM (n=64) curve is near ~2.60, the orange SepLLM (n=64) curve is near ~2.52, the green SepLLM (n=64, H) curve is near ~2.51–2.52, the red SepLLM (n=64, H/T) curve is near ~2.49, and the dark-blue SepLLM (n=128) curve is near ~2.55.
